title: A deceptively quiet galaxy
caption: The starburst galaxy NGC 3077, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3077 · constellation Ursa Major · about 13 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Light from many huge young star clusters blazes at the center of NGC 3077 in this Hubble image, and dusty tendrils lace the whole galaxy. Vast numbers of individual stars also appear across the frame, along with a few far more distant galaxies seen right through NGC 3077.

At first glance NGC 3077 resembles a typical, fairly peaceful elliptical galaxy. Hubble reveals otherwise, showing a hotbed of very energetic star formation. It lies about 13 million light-years away in Ursa Major, the Great Bear, forming a triplet with two brighter neighbors, the graceful spiral Messier 81 and the peculiar starburst galaxy Messier 82.

Interactions among the three galaxies have stoked star formation in the core of NGC 3077. Though overshadowed by its neighbors, it is very active too, and looks like a toned-down version of Messier 82.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.24 x 3.33 arcminutes) and distance (13 million light years), the frame spans roughly 12,000 × 13,000 light-years. Its light set out about 13 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. A blue filter is colored blue, an orange filter green, and a near-infrared filter red.
understand.eye: The colors are shifted from natural hues, part of the data is near-infrared light we cannot see, and no eye could separate these individual stars.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: William Herschel first saw NGC 3077 in 1801 with his 47 cm telescope in England, as he was nearing the end of his sky surveys. Each filter in this image had an exposure of about 27 minutes, and the field of view spans about 3.3 arcminutes.
alt: A galaxy with a brilliant glowing center of young star clusters, laced with dusty tendrils and surrounded by countless individual stars.
